MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "Eagles felt like the strongest choice because the country-rock songwriting and guitar work connect with the blues and roots rock I've been listening to.",
    "The Lovin' Spoonful and Wanted The Outlaws touched on the folk-rock and rootsy sounds I enjoy, even though neither made me want to choose another album today."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "25 and In The Lonely Hour lean toward pop ballads rather than the guitar-focused blues and roots sound I want right now.",
    "Bread felt too mellow for my current mood, while Patsy Cline's classic country vocals weren't the part of country-rock that attracted me to the Eagles.",
    "Stages and Partners gave me no clear connection to my recent listening, so I had little reason to try them on a visit when I'm only choosing one album."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "The choices seemed to assume that an interest in older rock also means wanting older pop hits, but Lesley Gore doesn't offer the bluesy connection I'm after.",
    "Several greatest-hits collections seemed to treat familiar songs as enough of a match, when the sound and guitar work matter more to me than familiarity."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "My recent listening points toward blues, roots rock, and expressive guitar playing; I wanted more choices that carry those qualities together.",
    "There's a difference between music that loosely fits my taste and something I'll choose today: mellow rock and rootsy country can appeal, but this visit I wanted the stronger guitar-and-songwriting fit of the Eagles."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "You caught some of my roots-rock interest, but stretched it too broadly into older hits and vocal pop instead of focusing on the guitar-driven sound I want now."
}
